additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional disorder is characterized by one or more non-bizarre or less obviously bizarre delusions lasting at least one month, in the absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized thought, or marked mood episodes that would suggest schizophrenia or a primary mood disorder with psychotic features. Outside of the delusional beliefs, functioning can be relatively preserved, and behavior often appears normal unless directly influenced by the delusional system. Onset is typically in mid to late adulthood and the course is often chronic, with beliefs remaining fixed despite clear contradictory evidence and limited insight. Subtypes may center on themes such as persecution, jealousy, erotomania, or somatic concerns, and clinicians distinguish delusional disorder from culturally sanctioned beliefs by assessing idiosyncrasy, rigidity, and the degree of functional impairment or interpersonal conflict produced by the delusions.

patient.stressor: About fourteen months ago, during a period of restructuring at his IT department and talk of outsourcing tech support, Joselito began to interpret ordinary glitches and policy changes as part of a targeted effort against him. Over the following year, as he continued mentoring junior staff and writing for a senior tech newsletter, these ideas hardened into a fixed conviction that certain coworkers were covertly monitoring his computer projects and trying to sabotage his reputation, even when audits and HR investigations found no irregularities. His late-night over-planning and coffee-fueled troubleshooting gradually centered more on documenting perceived plots than on actual technical problems, creating tension with colleagues and minor performance concerns despite his otherwise intact skills. He finally agreed to see a psychiatrist after his wife, worried by his insistence that the company was secretly building a case to fire only him and his refusal to accept reassurances from supervisors, asked their primary care doctor for a referral.
patient.chief_complaint: “My job says everything is fine, but I know certain people at work are secretly working against me and I can’t be convinced otherwise.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Even though HR and my supervisor keep telling me everything checks out, I’m completely convinced a couple of guys on my team are quietly logging into my tickets, tweaking things to make me look incompetent, and feeding that to management so they can eventually push me out, and no amount of reports or reassurances has shaken that belief.

add_requirements.functioning_not_markedly_impaired_apart_: Outside of all this worry about coworkers sabotaging me, I still handle my usual support tickets, mentor the junior staff, and write my regular pieces for the tech newsletter without any trouble.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because I’m so focused on tracking what I think they’re doing to undermine me, I’ve started spending extra hours documenting every little thing and double-checking work that was already fine, which has slowed me down and led my supervisor to mention slight concerns about my efficiency and tension with a couple of teammates.
add_requirements.duration: These ideas about people at work secretly working against me have been going on pretty steadily since the restructuring started a little over a year ago.
